# ByteTips

> Short, practical how-to guides for developers: JSON, JWT, images, CSS, and everyday privacy. Each post gives the answer, a code example, and a link to a free tool that does the job in your browser.

## Guides

- [How to Count Tokens Before Sending a Prompt to an LLM](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-count-tokens-before-prompting-llm/): Estimate token usage before prompting, so you stay inside context limits and control cost.
- [How to Compress Images Without Losing Quality](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-compress-images-without-losing-quality/): Shrink image file size while keeping them sharp, with the right format and quality settings.
- [How to Encode Text to Base64](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-encode-text-to-base64/): Encode and decode Base64 text in JavaScript and online.
- [How to Convert Text Case: camelCase, snake_case, and kebab-case](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-convert-text-case/): Convert identifiers between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, PascalCase, and more.
- [How to Use Regex in JavaScript](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-use-regex-in-javascript/): Test and learn regular expressions with live matching in JavaScript.
- [How to Format JSON in JavaScript](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-format-json-in-javascript/): Pretty-print, validate, and fix JSON in JavaScript and online.
- [What Is a JWT? How to Decode One Safely](https://bytetips.tech/posts/what-is-jwt-decode-safely/): Decode a JSON Web Token without sending it to a server, and check its claims.
- [How to Convert HEIC Photos to JPG](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-convert-heic-to-jpg/): Convert iPhone HEIC photos to JPG or PNG in the browser, no upload needed.
- [PX to REM: Why It Matters and How to Convert](https://bytetips.tech/posts/px-to-rem-why-it-matters/): Convert pixels to REM units for accessible, scalable CSS.
- [How to Remove EXIF Data from Photos Before Sharing](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-remove-exif-data-from-photos/): Strip location and device metadata from photos before posting them.
- [Fix "Unexpected token < is not valid JSON"](https://bytetips.tech/posts/fix-unexpected-token-not-valid-json/): Diagnose the fetch bug where HTML arrives instead of JSON — usually a wrong URL or an error page.
- [encodeURI vs encodeURIComponent: When to Use Each (and the Double-Encoding Trap)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/encodeuri-vs-encodeuricomponent/): encodeURI is for a whole URL, encodeURIComponent is for one value inside it — mix them up and you get broken links or %2520 double-encoding.
- [How to Check If a JWT Is Expired (the exp Claim)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-check-if-jwt-is-expired/): Read the exp claim, compare it with the current time, and avoid the seconds-vs-milliseconds trap.
- [How to Convert YAML to JSON: Python, Node, yq, and Online (Without Uploading Secrets)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/convert-yaml-to-json/): Parse YAML with yaml.safe_load, js-yaml, or yq -o=json — plus what gets lost: comments, anchors, and yes/no coercion.
- [Invisible Characters Are Breaking Your Code: How to Find and Remove Them](https://bytetips.tech/posts/invisible-characters-breaking-your-code/): Zero-width spaces and hidden Unicode sneak in through copy-paste and silently break string comparisons, logins, and builds — here is how to spot and strip them.
- [HEX to RGB: How the Conversion Actually Works](https://bytetips.tech/posts/hex-to-rgb-how-conversion-works/): A hex color is three base-16 numbers — split into pairs, convert each to decimal, and watch out for the shorthand and alpha traps.
- [How to Convert an Image to Base64 (Data URI)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-convert-image-to-base64/): A data URI embeds an image's bytes directly in HTML or CSS as data:image/png;base64,... — perfect for tiny icons, terrible for photos. Here is when to use it and when to skip it.
- [UUID v4 vs v7: Which Should You Use?](https://bytetips.tech/posts/uuid-v4-vs-uuid-v7/): UUID v4 is 122 bits of pure randomness; v7 starts with a millisecond timestamp so IDs sort by creation time. Use v4 by default, v7 for database primary keys.
- [How to Reduce SVG File Size](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-reduce-svg-file-size/): Most SVG bloat is decimal precision, editor metadata, and unused definitions. Run SVGO and you will typically cut 30–70% with zero visual change.
- [How to Create a Favicon for Your Website](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-create-a-favicon/): One square source image, four sizes, three link tags: 16 and 32px for tabs, 180px for Apple touch icons, 192 and 512px for PWAs.
- [How to Convert JSON to CSV (Python, jq, and Online)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-convert-json-to-csv/): JSON converts cleanly to CSV when it is an array of flat objects — here is the Python, pandas, and jq for it, plus what to do with nested data.
- [How to Create the Glassmorphism Effect with CSS](https://bytetips.tech/posts/glassmorphism-css-effect/): Five CSS properties make the frosted-glass look: a translucent background, backdrop-filter blur and saturate, a thin light border, rounded corners, and a soft shadow.
- [How to Convert AVIF to JPG](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-convert-avif-to-jpg/): AVIF files are 30–50% smaller than JPG but won't open everywhere — here's how to convert them (including batch) and what happens to transparency.
- [How to Use CSS box-shadow (Every Value Explained)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/css-box-shadow-explained/): box-shadow takes offset-x, offset-y, blur, spread, color, and an optional inset — here's what each value does, plus copy-paste recipes and the traps.
- [How to Convert Multiple PNGs to JPG at Once](https://bytetips.tech/posts/batch-convert-png-to-jpg/): Drop a folder of PNGs into a batch converter at quality 80–90 and watch gigabytes become megabytes — with the transparency and quality traps to avoid.
- [How to Write Better AI Prompts (a Reusable Template)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-write-better-ai-prompts/): Most bad AI output comes from vague input — the Role + Goal + Context + Output formula fixes it with four lines of structure.
- [WebP vs JPEG: Which Image Format Should You Use?](https://bytetips.tech/posts/webp-vs-jpeg/): WebP is 25–35% smaller than JPEG at the same quality and works in 97%+ of browsers — but JPEG still wins for email, print, and legacy software.
- [Password vs Passphrase: What's Actually Stronger?](https://bytetips.tech/posts/password-vs-passphrase/): Length beats complexity: a passphrase of four random words is stronger in practice than P@ssw0rd! — and you can actually remember it.
- [How to Encode HTML Entities (and Decode Them Back)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-encode-html-entities/): Swap & < > " ' for &amp; &lt; &gt; &quot; &#x27; so the browser shows text instead of parsing markup — plus the decode trick and the five traps.
- [How to Open HEIC Files on Windows](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-open-heic-files-on-windows/): Windows cannot open iPhone HEIC photos out of the box — convert them to JPG, install Microsoft's HEIF codec, or sync through the cloud.
- [How to Decode Base64 (Text, Images, Files, and the Common Errors)](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-decode-base64/): Decode Base64 with atob(), handle the Unicode trap with TextDecoder, fix padding and base64url, and decode data-URI images to Blobs.
- [How JWT Works: Header, Payload, Signature](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-jwt-works-header-payload-signature/): A JWT is three base64url parts — header, payload claims, signature. Signed, not encrypted; the signature proves the issuer, the encoding proves nothing.
- [How to Validate JSON Online](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-validate-json-online/): Valid JSON needs double quotes, no trailing commas, no comments — the 7 errors that break everything, how to read the error position, and schema validation.
- [PNG vs JPG: Which Image Format Should You Use?](https://bytetips.tech/posts/png-vs-jpg-which-format-to-use/): Photos go JPG at quality 80–85, graphics and anything with transparency go PNG — the lossy-vs-lossless decision list.

- [How to Fix 'CORS policy: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header'](https://bytetips.tech/posts/how-to-fix-cors-no-access-control-allow-origin/): CORS is the browser blocking your fetch, not the server rejecting it — simple requests vs preflight, and the fix for APIs you control vs ones you don't.
- [Fix 'ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR' in Localhost](https://bytetips.tech/posts/fix-err-ssl-protocol-error-localhost/): The browser tried HTTPS and the handshake failed — HTTP-vs-HTTPS mismatch, cached HSTS, bad local certificates, and how mkcert fixes the last one.
- [How to Fix 'Property does not exist on type' in TypeScript](https://bytetips.tech/posts/fix-property-does-not-exist-on-type-typescript/): TypeScript checks the declared type, not runtime shape — typos, vague types, union narrowing, and stale library types, with the fix for each.
- [HTTP Status Codes Explained](https://bytetips.tech/posts/http-status-codes-explained/): Read the first digit — 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error — plus the codes you'll actually meet, from 201 to 504.

## Tools

- [Byte-Kit](https://byte-kit.dev): 24 free developer tools that run entirely in your browser — JSON formatter, JWT decoder, Base64/URL encoder, regex tester, color converter, image compressor, HEIC converter, EXIF remover, and more. No uploads, no accounts.
